well thank you for asking that leads me to my second fun statistic: this is the IBDB page for William Shakespeare and if you notice that was the production of King Lear in 2019 but before that there was a five year gap without any Shakespeare plays on Broadway now five years might not sound like a lot but historically Shakespeare has been done on Broadway so frequently that you actually have to go back to the late 1800s before you can find a gap between two Shakespeare productions longer than five years and so this little gap here was actually quite historic and I know some of you are dying to go to my comments right now to be like “what about West Side Story?” “what about Kiss Me Kate?” “what about & Juliet?” “what about something rotten?” I'm not talking about adaptations or shows about Shakespeare I'm talking about actual productions of Shakespeare's plays so going back here for a second it's also worth noting that Kenny Leon is gonna become the first director of color to direct Shakespeare on Broadway in 30 years the last one being a production of the Tempest starring at Patrick Stewart which George C Wolf directed on Broadway in 1995 And while on the subject we are actually still in a very long drought since the last time a woman directed a Shakespeare play on Broadway the last time a woman was the sole credited director on a Shakespeare production on Broadway was in 1986 when Estelle Parsons directed a trio of Shakespeare plays running in rep although in 1988 Zoe Caldwell did receive a credit for “additional direction” for this production of MacBeth and this unusual credit was the result of one of many pieces of bizarre chaotic behind the scenes drama that plagued this production which the New York Times outlined in detail in this very entertaining article
